Withhold
with-hōld'
v. (to hold back; to keep from giving or doing)
From with in its old sense of against or back, and hold. To withhold is not merely to fail to give but to keep back something that was on its way — which is why Scripture treats it as an act, and judges it.

Biblical Definition

Two promises and two commands carry this word. The promise: “For the LORD God is a sun and shield: the LORD will give grace and glory: no good thing will he withhold from them that walk uprightly” (Psa 84:11). The comfort of that verse lies entirely in the word good. God withholds a great deal from His people, and the psalm does not deny it; it says that what He withholds is not good for them, on His judgment of good and not theirs. The prayer that answers it is David's: “Withhold not thou thy tender mercies from me, O LORD” (Psa 40:11). Then the commands, and both are about the hand. “Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, when it is in the power of thine hand to do it” (Pro 3:27) — a rebuke of the delayed wage, the deferred kindness, the good that is owed and postponed because postponement is cheap. And “Withhold not correction from the child” (Pro 23:13), where the good withheld is the painful kind. Ecclesiastes adds the labourer's form of it: “in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper” (Ecc 11:6). The pattern is consistent. God withholds by wisdom; man withholds by sloth, fear or greed.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines withhold as to hold back, to restrain, to keep from action; and to retain, to keep back, not to grant.

expand to see more

WITHHOLD, v.t. To hold back; to restrain; to keep from action.

1. To retain; to keep back; not to grant; as, to withhold assent to a proposition.

2. To keep; to maintain in possession; as, to withhold the wages of the hireling.

WITHHOLDEN, pp. Held back; restrained; kept from grant or exercise.

Key Scripture

Psa 84:11 — "For the LORD God is a sun and shield: the LORD will give grace and glory: no good thing will he withhold from them that walk uprightly."

Pro 3:27 — "Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, when it is in the power of thine hand to do it."

Psa 40:11 — "Withhold not thou thy tender mercies from me, O LORD: let thy lovingkindness and thy truth continually preserve me."

Ecc 11:6 — "In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good."

Modern Corruption

Psalm 84:11 is quoted as a promise of getting what one wants; the psalm makes God the judge of what is good.

expand to see more

No good thing will he withhold has been pressed into service as a guarantee of prosperity, health and the granting of desires, chiefly by the health-and-wealth teachers but also, more quietly, by ordinary believers doing their sums in the dark. The verse says something better and harder. It does not promise that God will withhold nothing; it promises that He will withhold no good thing, and it reserves to Him the determination of what is good. Paul asked three times for the thorn to be removed and was refused, and the refusal was the gift. A promise read the popular way collapses the first time a godly man buries a child; read as written, it survives the grave.

The command side is where the church has more to answer for. Proverbs 3:27 forbids the delay of good that is due and in the power of the hand — the unpaid worker, the unvisited widow, the reconciliation put off another year. James 5:4 says the hire kept back by fraud crieth, and the cries have entered into the ears of the Lord of sabaoth. Withholding is not passivity in Scripture; it is an act with a plaintiff.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew mana' (H4513), to withhold, keep back; chasak (H2820), to restrain, spare; Greek apostereo (G650), to defraud, to keep back what is owed.

expand to see more

Hebrew mana' (H4513) — to withhold, hold back, refuse; Psalm 84:11, Proverbs 3:27.

Hebrew chasak (H2820) — to restrain, hold back, spare; Proverbs 23:13, withhold not correction; Genesis 22:12, thou hast not withheld thy son.

Hebrew kala' (H3607) — to shut up, restrain; Psalm 40:11, withhold not thy tender mercies.

Greek apostereo (G650) — to defraud, to keep back wrongfully; James 5:4, the hire kept back by fraud.

Greek katecho (G2722) — to hold down, to restrain; 2 Thessalonians 2:6-7, of what withholdeth.

Usage

"“No good thing will he withhold” — and He decides what is good."

"“Withhold not good from them to whom it is due” — when the hand can do it now."

"“In the evening withhold not thine hand” — sow twice; you do not know which prospers."
